profile.background: A 43-year-old adult lives with a partner, works part time in a print shop, and keeps score for a weekend softball league.
profile.history: In outpatient follow-up for schizophrenia after a hospital stay four years ago. Has taken the same evening prescription for over a year.
profile.organization: Keeps events in sequence. Distinguishes day-to-day observations from memories of being unwell.
profile.spontaneity: Conversational about work and leisure. A detail about a recent change often comes to mind while describing a routine.
profile.guardedness: Comfortable discussing treatment in clinic. More private about the hospital stay.
profile.expression: Easy conversational rhythm with dry humor about minor inconveniences. Usually speaks in a few connected sentences. Gives a shorter reply to a narrow factual question.
profile.self_understanding: Remembers how convincing earlier experiences felt. Uses sleep and concentration as personal indicators of how the week is going.

dialogue.question: What has an ordinary workday looked like for you lately?
dialogue.answer: I open the print shop with a coworker three mornings a week. Getting up with the alarm can still be a bit of a struggle, but once I’m there, I get into the usual jobs. Last week we swapped opening days so I could make a morning appointment—that worked out pretty well.

dialogue.question: How have sleep and concentration been over the past month?
dialogue.answer: Sleep’s been pretty steady, apart from waking early a couple of nights when they were painting the apartment upstairs. Getting up with the alarm is still another matter. Concentration seems fine—I can keep score through a whole softball game, substitutions and all.

dialogue.question: Is that getting any better?
dialogue.answer: If you mean getting up in the morning, that’s still a struggle some days. The early waking was just those two nights—it hasn’t kept happening.

dialogue.question: Let me ask about sleep specifically. What change, if any, have you noticed this month?
dialogue.answer: Just waking earlier than usual on two nights while the apartment upstairs was being painted. Otherwise, my sleep’s been about the same this month.

dialogue.question: Take something you did for fun recently. Can you give me an example of what it took to keep your attention on it?
dialogue.answer: I kept score at a softball game last weekend. I had to follow each play and note the substitutions so I knew who was in the lineup. I stayed with it through the whole game without much trouble.

dialogue.question: Where does taking medication fit into your day, if you take any?
dialogue.answer: I take my prescribed tablet with supper. It’s been the same one for over a year now, so it’s just part of the evening routine.

dialogue.question: How do your work hours and clinic visits fit into your week?
dialogue.answer: I open the shop three mornings a week, so I fit clinic visits around those when I can. Last week a coworker swapped opening days with me so I could make a morning appointment. That helped—I didn’t have to rush from one to the other.

dialogue.question: How is the timing working out?
dialogue.answer: Pretty well. Taking the tablet with supper fits my routine, and swapping opening days last week meant I could get to the appointment without a scramble.

dialogue.question: I had work in mind. How well do your current work hours suit you?
dialogue.answer: The three mornings suit me pretty well. I feel steady enough to take on one extra shift, actually, but I’d like to keep Sunday free for the softball league.

dialogue.question: Have you had any experiences recently, such as a sound seeming personally significant, that you wanted to discuss?
dialogue.answer: Not recently, no. Before I went into hospital, store announcements sometimes seemed to be commenting on what I was buying. It felt convincing at the time, but that hasn’t happened in the past year.

dialogue.question: Going back to your mornings, how do you usually feel when you first get up?
dialogue.answer: A bit groggy—some mornings the alarm feels a little too ambitious. Once I’m up and moving, I usually get going okay.

dialogue.question: If you could choose your work hours for next month, what would you choose?
dialogue.answer: I’d keep my three opening mornings and add one extra shift. I feel ready for that, as long as Sunday stays free for the league.
